corrected_proposal.title: Kushner's Initial SF-86 Omitted Foreign-Government Contacts
corrected_proposal.description_short: Kushner's initial SF-86 omitted foreign-government contacts; the 100+ figure was reported later.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: Jared Kushner’s initial SF-86 was submitted on January 18, 2017, and omitted foreign-government contacts, according to his later statement and his lawyer’s comments to Politico. He said supplemental information followed the next day. The figure of more than 100 contacts was reported in July 2017, so it does not belong to the record’s May 25 date.
corrected_proposal.description_long: Jared Kushner submitted his initial SF-86 security questionnaire on January 18, 2017. In a July statement to the Senate Judiciary Committee, he said the filing was a rough draft submitted prematurely after his assistant misunderstood a message; the form did not list any foreign-government contacts. He said supplemental information was sent the next day. His explanation is attributed to him and does not independently establish why the form was incomplete. On July 16, Politico quoted Kushner’s attorney Jamie Gorelick saying the original submission omitted all contacts with foreign-government officials and that later materials included more than 100 calls or meetings with representatives of more than 20 countries. That later figure should not be assigned to the May 25 date in the source record: it was reported in July, months after the initial form. This repair dates the event to the January 18 filing and places the 100+ figure in the later supplementation context. The available material establishes the omission and reported correction, but not deliberate concealment, any particular clearance outcome, or the original synopsis’s suggestion that the contacts materially affected the FBI counterintelligence inquiry.

corrected_proposal.title: Trump Signs Order Creating Schedule Policy/Career for Policy-Influencing Positions
corrected_proposal.description_short: EO 14171 renamed Schedule F as Schedule Policy/Career for limited policy-influencing jobs; sources do not establish 50,000 removals on January 20, 2025.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14171, which renamed Schedule F as Schedule Policy/Career for a limited set of policy-influencing career positions. OPM later implemented the category through rulemaking. The supplied evidence does not support the original claim that 50,000 or more employees had already lost civil-service protections on January 20, so that figure and completed-removal framing are removed.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14171, “Restoring Accountability to Policy-Influencing Positions Within the Federal Workforce.” The order revived and amended the earlier Schedule F framework, renaming the category Schedule Policy/Career. The official rule description says it applies to a limited set of policy-influencing positions that are confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating. OPM later implemented the category through rulemaking; its description says covered roles remain career positions but are no longer subject to the same removal procedures. The order’s signature was a completed presidential action, but it does not establish that 50,000 employees had already been reclassified or lost protections on that date. The original entry’s estimate of 50,000-plus employees, claim of immediate removals across agencies, and “largest single rollback” characterization are therefore excluded. This record focuses on the order and the limited category it created, with later implementation treated as subsequent context. The number of positions ultimately designated and the number of employees actually affected are not established by the sources reviewed.
corrected_proposal.date_precision: Executive order signing date; later implementation is subsequent context.
corrected_proposal.category_assessment: Preserves the supplied category; Government Power Abuse is provisional and describes the reduction in removal procedures for a limited subset, not a finding of unlawful conduct.
